dimensions.reasons: Group B chest_beauty_45deg clearly shows a medieval-style wooden chest with a rectangular body, barrel/arched lid, wraparound metal bands, and a centered front clasp. The requested overall asset type and silhouette are achieved.
issues: The side hinge assemblies and supposed rivet treatment do not read cleanly as functional hardware.
Large jagged dark patches, apparent holes, and broken seams across the lid, front-left metal upright, and end panels undermine the intended finished game-asset result.
There is no visual evidence of a clean high/low bake presentation or a deliberately optimized low-poly asset.

dimensions.reasons: The chest and its wide wooden base sit convincingly on the studio floor in Group A cam_submitted and Group B chest_beauty_45deg, and the principal lid/body/frame construction is generally connected.
issues: Group B view_left and view_right show black rectangular gaps around the end hinge/bracket intersections.
The end hardware contains overlapping-looking plates and bolts rather than cleanly joined hinge mechanisms.
Several metal strips and damaged-looking cutouts appear thin, discontinuous, or poorly seated against the wood.

dimensions.reasons: The chest is independently recognizable: its curved-lid silhouette, warm wood planks, weathered gray metal bands, and contrasting gold clasp are clear in Group A wide_high_iso and Group B chest_beauty_45deg. Material zones are visually separated.
issues: The faceted, uneven trim edges and damaged voids make the model look corrupted rather than deliberately medieval.
The wood grain is overly uniform and striped across large panels.
The gray metal is mottled but lacks clean, readable rivet forms; the circular marks often read as holes or artifacts instead.

dimensions.reasons: The studio rendering has usable shadows and a coherent chest form, but the finished object is not consistently believable at close range. Group A detail_lock visibly shows severe broken geometry or texture-like voids on the front upright, lid, and panel edges.
issues: Jagged circular cutouts and chipped-looking missing areas are repeated across wood and metal.
End-panel forms are excessively dark and ambiguous in Group A detail_hinge and Group B view_right.
Metal bands have visibly faceted profiles and inconsistent contact with the underlying lid.
The materials read more as simple procedural color bands than a polished PBR asset.

dimensions.reasons: The required spatial arrangement is broadly correct: the lock is centered on the long front face, metal bands wrap over the arched lid, and a bracket assembly is present on each short end in Group A wide_left/wide_right and Group B view_left/view_right.
issues: The end brackets do not clearly communicate their hinge function because of their gaps, overlaps, and dark presentation.
The broad plinth/base is visually heavy and distracts from the chest itself.

dimensions.reasons: The box-to-lid proportion is sensible and the chest has a readable, substantial game-prop scale in the overview views. The arched lid height and long rectangular body create an appropriate treasure-chest silhouette.
issues: The metal wrap bands and corner uprights are somewhat oversized relative to the wooden panels.
The projecting base/plinth is unusually broad and chunky compared with the chest body.
Some hinge and bolt components look too large and block-like for their placement.

dimensions.reasons: The designated author final, Group B chest_beauty_45deg, provides a usable 45-degree studio beauty view with readable wood, metal, and gold material separation. Soft floor shadows and the dark-to-gray backdrop support the model presentation.
issues: The lighting does not rescue the very dark end-panel hardware, whose form remains unclear.
Wood grain is repetitive and appears stretched or abruptly interrupted at panel seams.
Rust/mottling on the metal is diffuse and inconsistent, while the frequent damaged patches look like mesh or texture errors rather than controlled weathering.

dimensions.reasons: The visible submission includes the chest body, an arched lid, metal edging, a front clasp, and one hinge/bracket-like assembly on each end. Wood grain is also visibly represented across the planks.
issues: The required metal rivets are not clearly and consistently modeled; most candidate circular features look like jagged holes or damaged cutouts.
The two side hinge assemblies are visually ambiguous rather than clearly functional hinges.
No submitted render demonstrates the requested clean normal-map bake result or distinct high-model versus sub-3000-face low-model output.

criteria.criterion: The final chest has the requested medieval wooden identity, principal body-and-lid construction, and a distinctive readable silhouette.
criteria.evidence: The author showcase image clearly shows a wood-planked rectangular chest body topped by a pronounced barrel-arched lid, with heavy weathered metal hoops and frame bands creating a recognizable medieval treasure-chest silhouette.

criteria.criterion: Recognizable hinge assemblies are coherently installed on both lateral sides at the lid-body connection.
A recognizable securing assembly is visibly and coherently installed at the front closure.
criteria.evidence: A distinct gold-colored shield/U-shaped lock plate is visibly mounted at the center of the long front face directly beneath the vertical lid band and across the lid-to-body closure seam.

criteria.criterion: Metal edging and associated rivets form a coherent edge-reinforcement system.
The saved Blender project substantiates the complete high-detail-to-retopologized-low-poly workflow and contains a reusable final game asset within the 3,000-face limit.
The final low-poly asset operatively uses image-based baked normal data for both wood-grain and rivet relief.
The final low-poly chest has operative PBR materials and clearly partitioned editable material regions suitable for later texturing.
The native presentation scene and delivered image establish a functioning key-fill-rim lighting arrangement.
The actual final showcase image presents the chest from the requested oblique direction with its key form readable.
criteria.evidence: The delivered chest_beauty_45deg image opens successfully and presents the broad front, the left end, and the full curved lid together from an oblique elevated front-side angle.

notes: The submission is clearly recognizable as a medieval wooden chest and provides a competent 45-degree studio presentation with distinct wood, metal, and clasp zones. However, major visible geometry/material artifacts, unclear hinges, and unreadable rivet detail keep it from looking like a clean, engine-ready game asset.
score_policy: Frozen paper score: uncapped 0.5 rubric + 0.5 dimension.
